items_missed: No 'How are you today?' - jumped straight from the name capture into the profile pull.

Entire Save Your Ass prep speech missing - never told him prep before move day shortens the move and lowers the bill, no consolidation examples (kids' toys, loose drawer items, photos off walls), no take-a-carload tip.
No visual equivalent used to help him picture truck capacity or scope (school bus reference or similar).
Never mentioned the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email.
Insurance explanation covered No Worries but not the 60 cents/lb baseline coverage.
Used the customer's name only twice (confirming his full name and at the sign-off) - short of 3+ uses through the call.
top_strength: Textbook probe and pricing execution - she covered all 11 probe items including the stressor question, then delivered the full differentiator block (No Worries, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee) and the complete no-hidden-fees list without missing a beat. The TV handling was the standout: she caught that the 70-inch had no box, explained the blanket wrap, and proactively volunteered that the 55-inch goes in a TV case at no charge.
coaching_note: Everything is in place except Save Your Ass - that one missing block is 10 of the 17 points she dropped. Add the prep speech right after the estimate and before the booking ask, and this call clears mastery.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm and accommodating language ('go ahead, take your time', 'no fees for that', 'glad to hear'), acknowledged what he said before moving on, and closed using his name - held back from a 5 only by how often 'Awesome' repeats verbatim and the absence of any real rapport moment.
